rows.description: Younger relatives ask about careers and life. Share your experience with humility, avoid pushing your path as the only one, and connect them to resources. Listening to what they want matters more than advising.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: admiration, dependence, envy, pride

rows.description: A mistake from years ago still plays in your head. Own the harm, make amends if possible, and then allow yourself to move on. Endless self-punishment helps no one; learning and changed behaviour do.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: forgiveness, resentment

rows.description: You understand your parents' limits as young adults and see their own struggles. Forgiveness may mean release of resentment, not excusing harm. Set boundaries where needed and appreciate the effort they made.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: guilt, resentment

rows.description: A former friend or partner hurt you badly. Forgiving is for your peace; it need not mean reconciliation or trust. Let go of revenge fantasies, keep safe distance, and be willing to accept an apology if it is real.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: guilt, resentment
related mind states: calm, trust, hurt

rows.description: Someone you wronged reaches out with anger. Listen without defending, apologise specifically without demanding forgiveness, and offer repair if wanted. Forgiveness is theirs to give in their own time.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: forgiveness, resentment

rows.description: Replaying old insults keeps you tied to them. Resentment is like carrying heat to throw at someone else. Speak with a friend or counsellor, decide what you need, and free yourself even if they never apologise.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: forgiveness, guilt

rows.description: Someone who hurt you offers a sincere apology. Notice whether it names what they did and changes behaviour. You may accept it without restoring full trust, and take time before deciding.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: forgiveness, guilt, resentment

rows.description: After a big win, you feel superior and hear praise constantly. Enjoy it and remember luck, teachers and support. Stay curious and listen to critics, since ego hardens when no one challenges you.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: envy, fear, gratitude, manipulation

rows.description: The success was built by others, too. Thank them by name, share credit and rewards, and mention their contributions to senior leaders. A leader who takes all the credit slowly loses trusted people.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: envy, fear, manipulation, pride

rows.description: A friend congratulates you but seems sour, or teases you about your new status. Stay humble, avoid showing off, and keep the friendship anchored in shared history. Give them space, and share their wins too.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: fear, gratitude, manipulation, pride
